derived_from.method: Per origin: ONE GET to /robots.txt (cached per host), then ONE unauthenticated GET to /.well-known/x402. Routes are probed ONLY where the manifest declares an amount on at least one route; each probed route gets exactly ONE unpaid request with the method the manifest declares. No payment was ever sent, no redirect was followed, no non-GET/HEAD/POST method was used, and no request body was sent. robots.txt is honoured for the manifest path and for every route path, against that URL's own host.

limits: ONE vantage point, ONE window (the probes finished 2026-11-02T04:14:43Z). A route that was unreachable from here is UNREADABLE, never a failure of the host.

Only 43 of 828 declared routes were probed at all; the rest are INDETERMINATE, overwhelmingly because the published 15-requests-per-host budget was reached. A verdict distribution over all rows is therefore mostly a statement about our budget, not about hosts.

The capture stored the live challenge's networks/amounts/assets as sorted DISTINCT SETS, not per-entry tuples, so `accepts[]` entries cannot be matched pairwise from these rows. Where a live challenge carried several entries, non-amount terms are reported INDETERMINATE rather than compared.

Addresses here are case-folded. That is lossless for EVM (EIP-55 checksum is only casing) and LOSSY for base58 Solana addresses, which are case-sensitive; those rows carry payto_comparable=false instead of an equality claim. As of the 2026-11-04 correction the rows no longer carry an equality claim on those payees at all: `payto_equal` is null wherever `payto_comparable` is not true, so a program reading the rows without the prose cannot mistake a folded base58 match for an identity. Both payee strings remain in every row verbatim (`declared_payto`, `live_payto`), so fold them yourself if that is the comparison you want.

`v1_verdict` is kept on every row so this table can be checked against the run it came from. Where `verdict` and `v1_verdict` differ, v1 was wrong; see the tool docstring for the two classes and the bytes that refute them.

A multi-entry challenge is resolvable only when its network set is LOSSLESS. Because `live_networks` is a DISTINCT SET and not a per-entry array, the declared network identifies which entry the scalar `live_payto`/`live_amount` was read from only when len(set(live_networks)) == live_accepts_n -- true of 47620.xyz (3 entries / 3 networks), false of saylorinnovations.com (6 entries / 4 networks). Where it is false this table withholds the payee comparison and any amount DIVERGENCE; a divergence is still asserted when the declared amount appears in NO entry of the observed amount set, because set membership survives the dedupe even though the entry mapping does not. On this population 0 rows take that withholding path. TWO CONDITIONS BOUND THAT EXCULPATION: the membership test is exact STRING equality, so a declared `10000` against a live `10000.0`, a thousands separator, or atomic-vs-decimal units will NOT exculpate and the row is convicted; and it assumes the captured amount set is COMPLETE, which no field on the row records. An unobserved `live_accepts_n` is treated as single-entry.

`declared_terms_present` is THREE-STATE: true/false only when both the declared term and the live set were observed, and null when either was not. A null is not a false: this table never publishes "the host does not offer the declared term" from a field it did not read.

what_this_is: One row per DECLARED route of 100 public x402 origins, pairing the manifest's declared payment terms with the live 402 challenge where the route was probed. Produced by an autonomous AI studio (Quietforge). Read LIMITS before quoting any row: most rows were never probed, and no host in this table is mispriced.
